external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser that accesses the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.
external_entities.notes: The browser is outside the system's network.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application that receives browser traffic and places jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: Web application with a queue-decoupled background process.
processes.notes: The web application does not do the heavy work itself.

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: A background worker that picks up jobs and performs the heavy work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.
processes.notes: The background worker reads and writes the database.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue onto which the web application puts jobs and from which the background worker picks them up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up and does the work.
data_stores.notes: The diagram does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database used by the background worker; it also stores the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The diagram does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: The configuration store containing the web application's settings and queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config
data_stores.notes: The diagram does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: The configuration store containing the worker's settings and database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config
data_stores.notes: The diagram does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_flows.name: talks
data_flows.description: The browser talks to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say anything about how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: picks them up
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: reads and writes
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say anything about how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from the web application config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from the worker config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet outside the system's network, where the user's browser sits.

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The network tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The network tier containing the queue, worker and database behind the web tier.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source says that a user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker has internal exposure because it is in the backend tier behind the web tier.
assumptions.basis: The source places the worker in the backend tier behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a queue-decoupled background worker process that picks up jobs and does work.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds the web application's queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source says the web application config holds the credentials the process needs, including queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds the worker's database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source says the worker config holds the credentials the process needs, including database credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The public internet, web tier and backend tier are separate network trust boundaries because the source identifies them as distinct network locations.
assumptions.basis: The source distinguishes the public internet from the system's network.

assumptions.assumption: The web tier is a network trust boundary because it is identified as a distinct tier from the backend tier.
assumptions.basis: The source says the web application runs in the web tier and places the queue, worker and database in the backend tier behind it.

assumptions.assumption: The backend tier is a network trust boundary because it is identified as a distinct tier behind the web tier.
assumptions.basis: The source says the queue, worker and database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.
